summary: Legacy VB6 application with critical modernization needs: COM dependencies, potential SQL injection risks, and outdated UI patterns requiring comprehensive refactoring

hotspots.reason: Legacy ADO 2.5 COM objects create deployment and security vulnerabilities
VB6 event-driven architecture requires complete restructuring for web-based implementation
Login form suggests custom authentication without modern security standards
Client-side VB6 validation needs server-side implementation with proper sanitization

risks.title: COM Dependency Obsolescence
risks.description: ADO 2.5 and other COM references will not function in .NET Core environment

risks.title: SQL Injection Vulnerability
risks.description: Legacy ADO patterns likely use string concatenation for SQL queries

risks.title: Authentication Security Gap
risks.description: Custom VB6 authentication lacks modern security features like MFA, token-based auth

risks.title: UI Behavior Preservation Challenge
risks.description: MDI interface and VB6 control events require careful mapping to web UI patterns
